subject.title: Multi-profile profile targeting/config truth is ambiguous with ~/.openclaw-* homes on macOS

question: What should the macOS profile-targeting contract be when an explicit root `--profile` conflicts with inherited LaunchAgent identity, profile casing, or separate `~/.openclaw-*` homes?
rationale: The source-backed stale-label subcase is real, but choosing how explicit profiles interact with custom launchd labels, case-sensitive profile names, and mixed home layouts changes supported operator behavior.

options.title: Make explicit profile authoritative
options.body: Treat root `--profile` as the service/config/session target, clear only stale OpenClaw-managed launchd labels, and add clearer status output plus live macOS proof.

options.title: Preserve label override precedence
options.body: Keep `OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL` as the stronger targeting signal and document nested cross-profile lifecycle commands as unsupported or requiring explicit env cleanup.

options.title: Defer to broader profile design
options.body: Keep this issue open as a product-design umbrella until maintainers decide casing, mixed-home, service-label, and status truth together.

recommendation.title: Make explicit profile authoritative
recommendation.body: Treat root `--profile` as the service/config/session target, clear only stale OpenClaw-managed launchd labels, and add clearer status output plus live macOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail points most strongly to steipete for profile-aware service naming and the multi-gateway guide that define the current operator contract.
